summary: The article surveys cutting-edge US and European Big Pharma innovation in oncology, diabetes/obesity, HIV and Alzheimer's, aimed at Indian investors seeking exposure to pharma. It closes with a framework for assessing US pharma stocks (expiring drugs, ramping drugs, pipeline) and reiterates recommendations on Novo Nordisk and Abbvie, with a positive view on Merck despite Keytruda's 2028 patent loss.
one_line: Overview of Big Pharma breakthroughs in cancer, diabetes, HIV and Alzheimer's, plus a framework and stock picks (Novo Nordisk, Abbvie, Merck) for investors.
key_facts: Merck's Keytruda (pembrolizumab), approved in 2014, generated $20 billion in sales in 2022 and works by blocking the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction between cancer cells and T-cells.
Treatment-resistant patient cohorts to monoclonal antibodies (mABs) stood at 70-80 per cent.
Gilead acquired Immunomedics for $20 billion for its ADC Trodelvy; Merck paid $4 billion upfront to Daiichi Sankyo to collaborate on ADCs.
The US FDA has approved 10 ADCs for cancer treatment, with more than 80 ADCs in clinical trials.
In CAR-T therapies, Celgene acquired Juno Therapeutics for $9 billion and Gilead acquired Kite Pharma for $12 billion.
Novo Nordisk's Wegovy (semaglutide) showed 17-18 per cent weight loss over 68 weeks in obese patients, and semaglutide reduced adverse cardiovascular events by 20 per cent in overweight patients.
Novo Nordisk launched Rybelsus, a pill version of its GLP-1RA, while Pfizer and Eli Lilly have joined the weight-loss race.
Gilead's Lenacapavir, approved last year, is a single-pill regimen for HIV patients with multi-drug resistance; a February 2023 study showed 90 per cent virological suppression at 26 weeks.
Leqembi (lecanemab), developed by Eisai with Biogen, became the first and only approved Alzheimer's drug in July 2023, reducing clinical decline by 27 per cent at 18 months.
Biogen's adacanumab received accelerated FDA approval, prompting three advisers to resign over a drug that could cost $56,000 per annum.
Pharma assessment rests on drugs about to expire, drugs in ramp-up, and pipeline; Phase-I/II/III assets get 10/20/50 per cent probability of success.

Novo Nordisk (+140 per cent since July-21) and Abbvie (+27 per cent since Oct-21) are reiterated, trading at 31 times and 12 times FY24 earnings; Humira lost patent by end 2023 ($22 billion revenue in 2022).
Merck trades at 12 times FY24 EPS, with Keytruda's likely patent loss in 2028; investors can accumulate on dips.
Leqembi is expected to hit $7 billion peak sales by 2030 at a $26,500 annual list price; Biogen has a $33 billion market cap at 14 times FY24 EPS.
